newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish truckers stop strike for economic reasons.
newsitem.headline: Spanish truckers stop strike for economic reasons.

text.p: Truckers in Spain said on Wednesday they had called off a strike that had lasted two weeks after a meeting with government officials.

"It's been decided not to continue with the current work stoppage because of the economic consequences," Jose Maria Arambarri, a spokesman for the truckers' organisation leading the strike, told journalists. "There's been no type of deal."

The striking truckers reached the decision after a meeting with the government's director of land transport, Fernando Cascales, even though Fedatrans, the organisation leading the labour action, said there had been no overall accord.

"There didn't seem to be much sense in continuing to try to get pacts on concrete points," one of the truckers on the negotiating team said, adding that they were satisfied that Spaniards and the Development Ministry had understood the problems in the transport sector.

The tension between strikers and the government in the two-week-long labour action had appeared to be easing earlier on Wednesday as police re-opened roads and the affected industries, particularly carmakers, had started to cope with the strike.
The government welcomed the decision and said it was still open to dialogue with the truckers.
